projects.title: Show HN: Stoke Money – Personal finance app built around a cash flow forecast
projects.author: _wesley
projects.summary: Hi HN, I've been through many finance tracking apps, starting with Personal Capital, then Monarch, and most recently Copilot. None of them have worked perfectly for my needs. All of these apps tend to model “cash flow” as the net sum of your transactions during a month, yet while credit card charges are reported immediately, they are typically deducted from checking (cash) accounts the following month when the bill is due. As a result, I've always had to maintain a separate spreadsheet to track my actual cash flow. These apps also have a huge focus on managing budgets, which has never been for me. My spending is rarely consistent month-to-month, so every month I'm comparing my fully justified spending against my budget, and tweaking my budget until I “pass”. So I built yet another finance tracking app. It has the usual components - accounts, transactions, categories - but the core is a cash flow projection engine, and everything else is built around it. Budgets are gone. Instead, each income/spending category is projected forward from your historical activity, but not as a flat monthly number. They land in whatever account you historically use (e.g. checking account for paychecks/rent/bills, credit/debit cards for daily spending). Credit card payments are modeled automatically based on your projected credit card balance. You can set up your own recurring transfers between accounts as well, to model savings, for example. The end result is that the app can forecast how your cash moves, and you can see in advance when any account might run low. If all of your accounts look good for the next 12 months, maybe you don't have a budgeting problem. What’s made the biggest difference for me has been the MCP integration, which I have connected to Claude (but can be connected to any AI agent of your choice). I have asked it to import historical transactions by uploading PDF account statements, categorize/tag all transactions that took place while I was on vacation, and plan transfers across my accounts to cover expected payments. I hope some people that share my frustrations will find this app useful.

projects.title: 【产品自荐】usAge：支持 iOS、macOS、Android 和鸿蒙的 AI 用量查看工具
projects.author: chen2he
projects.summary: 自荐一款面向 AI 重度用户和独立开发者的小工具。 同时使用 Codex、Claude、Cursor 等工具时，经常需要分别打开各家的页面，才能知道额度用了多少、什么时候恢复。写代码写到一半碰到额度上限，也很打断节奏。 因此我做了 usAge，把分散在不同 AI 服务里的用量、余额和重置时间集中展示，还能放到桌面小组件上，随时看一眼。 usAge 的一大特色是多平台支持。 目前已上线 iPhone、iPad、Mac、Apple Watch、Android 和 HarmonyOS，可以在电脑工作时查看，也能在手机、平板或手表上随时掌握 AI 额度。各平台提供原生应用，并结合系统能力提供桌面小组件等快捷查看方式。 目前支持 Codex、Claude、Cursor、智谱 GLM、Kimi、MiniMax、Xiaomi MiMo、OpenRouter 和 DeepSeek，按各服务商提供的数据展示额度、余额或 Token 用量。 主要功能： 集中查看多个服务和账号：减少在不同后台之间来回切换。 桌面小组件：提供多种视觉样式，不打开 App 也能查看用量。 额度重置提醒：额度恢复后及时收到通知。 多平台使用：已上线 iOS、macOS、Android 和 HarmonyOS。 设备直接查询：用量请求由设备直接发往服务商，无需把服务商凭证交给 usAge 服务器。 usAge 采用免费版 + Pro 一次性买断的模式：免费版可以连接 1 个服务，Pro 解锁不限数量的服务连接，适合同时使用多家 AI 工具的人。 这是我独立开发、持续维护的产品。希望它能帮大家少花一点时间查额度，在安排 AI 编程任务、切换工具时更有数。 官网及下载： 欢迎体验，也欢迎反馈你最希望接入的服务和使用场景。谢谢！

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Agent Guard：给 AI 编程助手的破坏性操作加一味“后悔药”
projects.author: mokuyoaxis

github.name: mokuyoaxis/agent-guard
github.description: Make destructive AI-agent actions reversible by default — quarantine + audit + human escalation for rm/git destructive operations. Reliability infrastructure, not a sandbox.

projects.summary: 之前使用 AI 编程助手时，我遇到过一次子代理删掉 $HOME 的事故。这次经历让我发起了 Agent Guard，和社区合作者一起，尝试给 AI 的破坏性操作留条退路。 它的思路很直接：能安全执行的继续，能补偿的先留恢复余地，不确定的请求用户确认，无法安全处理的拒绝执行。 目前主要提供： 删除保护：受支持的删除操作先将有价值的文件移入隔离区，保留记录，方便之后查询和恢复。 Git 快照：在受支持的破坏性 Git 操作前，保存已跟踪文件的当前状态，保护尚未提交的修改。 外发检查：检查文本中支持的凭据类型和敏感路径，提供脱敏或拒绝输出的处理方式。 另外提供 guard-lab，用合成标记和一次性项目，对 Agent 行为进行有明确范围的观察与测试。 项目可通过 Skill／CLI 使用，也提供 Claude Code、Kimi Code、DSH 的可选 Hook 适配。自动拦截依赖宿主实际加载兼容 Hook，具体覆盖范围随工具、版本和配置而异。 MIT 开源，Core 需要 Python 3.9+ 和 Git，提供中文文档及 npm 安装包。欢迎反馈误报、漏报和宿主适配问题。 项目：GitHub · 中文文档与接入指南 · npm 安装包

projects.summary: bodycam 是一个免费开源的 macOS 工具，用系统自带的 eslogger（Endpoint Security）记录 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 等 AI 编程助手执行的每条命令、读写的每个文件、读取的密钥和打开的网络连接。 主要功能： 用 bodycam claude 启动助手，退出时生成 Markdown 报告，命令行里像 token 的值会自动打码。 标记值得注意的行为：读取 .env、SSH 私钥、钥匙串、浏览器数据，修改 .zshrc、LaunchAgents，执行 curl | sh 等。 连助手启动的子进程（npm test、shell 脚本）也一起记录，这些在助手自己的对话记录里看不到。 菜单栏应用：助手运行时图标变红，读到敏感文件时发通知，每次运行都有完整时间线。 bodycam --demo 运行一个无害的假助手，可以直接看效果。 报告只保存在本机。MIT 协议，Go + Swift 编写。 支持平台：macOS 13+（Apple Silicon 与 Intel） 安装： brew install omlahore/tap/bodycam brew install --cask omlahore/tap/bodycam-app 截图：

projects.title: Show HN: RDST – A local agent that watches Postgres/MySQL for query regressions
projects.author: gvsg
projects.summary: We noticed during the course of many many years of DBA related work that fixes to database issues and queries are always reactive. An entire database can fall over extremely quickly when an unbounded query grows without warning. Traditionally, DBAs hear complaints of slowness and follow a methodical process: - manually browse pg_stats or other database related performance internal tables - see which queries are slowest - figure out what indexes are missing - figure out which indexes are actually bad and slowing down writes - painstakingly implement a fix In the age of cheap intelligence, we decided that there is no reason we can’t have an always-on agent that is designed to do this job for you. Databases need something or someone that is always watching with a massive amount of contextual understanding to be able to take quick actions. We’ve watched the alternative play out repeatedly. One of our users’s checkout page went from loading instantly to taking 11 seconds in a single night with no code change. How? Well somehow their order table grew by 40M rows because BI team had injected historical data and suddenly postgres started doing full table scans. Sometimes routine operations have unintended results and can easily destroy your database. We wanted to catch these kinds of regressions instantly. So we built RDST. RDST is a desktop agent that runs on your PC and connects to PostgreSQL / MYSQL (read only) and compares every query against its own performance every minute. Every expensive query is automatically EXPLAIN ANALYZED, stripped of PII and sent to U.S. based frontier or open model providers to analyze which indexes are missing, how the query could be rewritten, and provides the fix. We then run a classifier model (JEV) to decide if you should be notified (is this standard behavior for this particular query?), and the full history of the query performance is kept for years. RDST also keeps track of your entire database health in general, and recommends more fixes than simply bad queries. Since it runs locally we can keep the database credentials stored in your OS Keychain (RDST never keeps them in its own storage layer), and the connection goes straight to your database (using a jump host or SSH tunnel for private connections). You can read more about how we handle data especially as it pertains to LLM use here. https://readyset.io/docs/readyset-ai/rdst/desktop/privacy We really want feedback from the community from people running Postgres and MySQL in production. We are giving inference away completely for free. Just as a reminder, RDST will NOT run any updates or indexes against your database at this time. We are considering a fully autonomous auto-pilot mode in the future, but for now we are leaving the actual fixes in your hands. Let us know what you think!

projects.title: 做了半年无审查 AI 平台，记 4 个反直觉的工程坑（都有数据）
projects.author: largep
projects.summary: 我在做一个中文 AI 创作平台（对话、图片、视频、音频都有）。半年下来，最大的收获不是功能，而是一堆反直觉的坑。挑 4 个有数据的分享一下，对做 AI 应用的朋友可能有用。 ## 1. 「无审查」往往卡在托管商，不在模型本身 同一个图片编辑模型 **Seedream V5 Pro**，放在三家托管商上，用 40 条容易触发审核的编辑指令和同一张原图逐条测试（ 2026 年 8 月实测），被内容策略拒绝的比例分别是 **0%、12.5% 和 90%**。模型是同一个，差别全在托管商自己加的那一层审核：有的托管商在接口上根本没有提供关闭安全检查的开关，有的审核是概率性的，同一句话重试一次可能就过了。 所以挑「无审查」服务时，看名字没用，要看它实际跑在哪家，实测拒绝率是多少。 ## 2. DeepInfra 的 TTS 一过 15 秒就变成白噪声 长文本语音合成时，大约 60 秒的音频会在中段突然变成刺耳的白噪声。 抓包后发现，DeepInfra 在一个本该是裸 PCM 数据的流里，每 15 秒左右插入一行 45 字节的 SSE 心跳： ``` : ping - \r\n\r\n ``` PCM16 一个采样占 2 字节，而 45 是奇数。心跳一插进去，后面所有采样的字节都错位了一位，听起来就是白噪声。解决办法是在流里识别并剥掉这一行。如果你也在用 DeepInfra 的流式 TTS ，可以检查一下 300 字以上的长文本。 ## 3. Vercel 函数冻结，会吞掉「发出去就不管」的写入 计量日志和服务端埋点我们最初是 fire-and-forget 写的（`void fetch(...)`，不 await ）。后来发现，Vercel 的函数实例在响应发出后就会被冻结，没写完的 promise 会被挂起，直到下一个请求把实例唤醒才继续，而那时连接早已超时。 丢不丢取决于写入能不能在响应发出前的几毫秒内完成：复用热连接的数据库 INSERT 多半能活下来，要新建 TLS 连接的埋点请求则基本必丢。所以高峰期几乎看不出问题，低谷期和单次调用会稳定地丢数据，统计结果在半夜系统性偏低。 解决办法是用 `@vercel/functions` 的 `waitUntil` 把这些 promise 包起来，实例会等它们完成再冻结。修好之后，单次调用并静默 150 秒，计量和埋点也都能在响应后约 200ms 内落地。如果你在 Vercel 上做统计，发现半夜的数据总是少一截，可以查查这个。 ## 4. 长对话越长，回复末尾越容易出现乱码 我们统计了某个无审查模型回复末尾出现乱码的比例，发现它随上下文长度单调上升：上下文在 8k token 以内时约 0.01%，超过 48k 时到了 1.95%。短对话根本复现不出来，所以一开始一直以为是偶发故障。 更麻烦的是，一旦历史里出现过一次乱码，模型会照着抄下去。把 temperature 调到 0.7 之后，这种「被污染的历史」引发的乱码从 7/40 降到了 1/40 。所以先调采样参数，比去砍上下文更有效。 --- ## 最后说点题外话 这个项目从头到尾都是几乎我一个人在做。半年下来最大的感受是：一个人靠技术挣钱，养活自己是可以的。前提是选一个大厂不愿意做、或者做不好的方向，然后把那些脏活累活一件件干完。上面这些坑，没有一个是写功能时想得到的。 工具方面，最想夸两家。Vercel 是真好用：每个分支自动部署一个预览环境，合并到主干就上线，一个人也能保持很快的发布节奏，上面那个冻结的坑算是我交的学费。Cloudflare 是真良心：对象存储不收出口流量费，图片和视频这种大流量业务能省下一大笔钱，连域名邮箱都是免费转发的。 --- 平台叫 [思畅 AI]( https://sichang.xyz ），网页端可以免费试用，也有兼容 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 接口的 API ，可以直接接 Claude Code 。 --- 4 月 [发过一帖]( https://v2ex.com/t/1204769 )，当时大家提的意见都记下了。模型方面，默认模型已经换掉了。隐私方面，我们不再做「不存储」这种没法验证的承诺，改为隐私和便利并重：对话保存在账号下，手机、电脑多台设备可以同时使用，消息实时同步；传输全程 HTTPS, 数据库静态加密，数据按账号隔离；对话不用于训练任何模型，可以随时一键导出或删除。这里不是端到端加密，想要绝对的隐私，本地模型仍然是最好的选择。 欢迎拍砖。

projects.title: Show HN: Turbo Lisp – A Common Lisp IDE for macOS and the Terminal
projects.author: stray
projects.summary: When Apple left Clozure Common Lisp behind by switching to Apple Silicon, I started kicking around the idea of building my own Lisp/Objective-C bridge by combining Apple Documentation, the clang AST, and introspection of the Objective-C runtime. There was a CCL porting effort, but I really wanted to use SBCL anyway. Truth be told — what I really wanted was a 21st-century CLIM variant on top of modern AppKit 26. So I let that idea rattle around in my skull for a while — and eventually it bounced up against the memory of Ck (Curses-based Tk). Anybody remember that? I liked Tcl/Tk and [incr Tcl] and it had always stuck in my head how great an idea it was to have something along the lines of CLIM for regular terminals as well as GUI. So anyway, I stumbled upon the open-source CLIM2 source still maintained by Franz, and the wheels commenced to turn. Oh yeah, and my very first programming environment had been Turbo Pascal. That integrated debugger was really something. And y'know, it all started to come together as an idea about modernizing CLIM and modifying Portable Hemlock to run on top of it — and integrating a Debugger with conditional breakpoints and Step In/Step Out/Step Over, CLIM presentations, Inspector... And in years past, I'd have just dreamed about it. But the past three years have been crazy. GPT4 was the first time I seriously tried to build things with an LLM. And I've been pushing the LLMs as far as they would go to build my intuition mainly. But up until this year they've been mostly crap. I used "Build Common Lisp" as my north star because the Dietz ANSI tests seemed like a nearly perfect product specification. Long story short: I threw away 7 attempts before I won ANSI — https://gitlab.com/patchwork1-ai/whateverlisp — and while I was waiting for Claude and Codex to grovel through ANSI I was trying my hand at my grand idea of Turbo Lisp. Side note: my high score on ANSI is 21,916/21,925 passing (99.96%); 21,925 executed; 9 failing. And those 9? Yeah I don't think you could pass those without failing 30+ other ones. So anyway — It’s called *Turbo Lisp* (based on SBCL). It brings together a Listener, debugger, object inspector, conditional breakpoints + stepper, and Zeta—a variant of Portable Hemlock that uses WhateverCLIM as its front-end. On macOS, it uses native AppKit UI through *Chattanooga, a Lisp/Objective-C bridge I built*. It also runs in the terminal through *Oak Ridge, my Lisp port of Ratatui*. Both use *WhateverCLIM*, which is the CLIM2 code from Franz plus my own modernization, including * presentations* : displayed Lisp objects you can click and inspect. *v0.2.1 patch release* is available for Apple Silicon Macs, Intel Macs, and Linux x86-64. The Mac builds currently require macOS 26. I’m especially interested in hearing: * Does it install and start properly on your machine? * Can you find your way around the Listener, editor, and debugger? * Does the terminal interface work with your terminal emulator? * Where does it feel confusing, awkward, or broken? A report that says “I tried this and got stuck here” is useful. Please include your OS, CPU architecture, and terminal emulator where relevant. projects.summary: Hi everyone! I'm Joe, and I built Tennis: a CLI that indexes and searches your context offline. You can index any files, your Chat & Claude sessions, Codex history, etc. All local and offline. I've always hated having chats siloed in Claude and not having an easy way to connect that context in other apps. Anything that exists today has a subscription and is stored on their servers, and really wanted something fast, local, and offline. How Tennis works: * SQLite/FTS5 (keyword) + vec0 (vector) * model2vec / potion-retrieval-32M (512-dim, 123MB). This is a flat vector table, and what helps make this work well local/offline. * RRF (k=60) fuses BM25 keyword rank + cosine semantic rank into one score Tennis also creates markdown files called 'cards' at indexing time. This gives you an easy, summarized, human readable format to see what Tennis has. You can edit these files (but won't change the embeddings in SQLite). You can use Tennis via API and MCP. It's incredibly fast, and the MCP works great as a connector to different applications (ChatGPT, Claude, Opencode, etc). You can install and use it today: https://tennis.jlachance1.workers.dev/ Thanks for checking this out! I would love any feedback. Thank you

What's cool is that beeline agents can automate _auth_ through trustysquire.ai - they can sign up to most services and APIs without you having to do it for them. - A new primitive called workflows, that are skills for teams of agents. - multi way call with your entire team, humans and agents. projects.summary: 今年想开一家实体店，需要经常找位置、查看周边情况。用高德有时候有点麻烦，记录自己的想法和实地照片也不太方便，所以自己写了一套选址工具。 注册即可体验： https://wash.ailibrary.space/ 基于高德 API 做的，侧重于快速查询周边情况，同时接入 Agent 来找位置和做评估。整体系统分为下面四个部分： ### 1. 地图选址 核心功能，可以定位查看周边 1 、3 、5 km 范围内的小区、商超等数据。 另外，基于 WorldPop 人口模型数据做了人口热力图，还能查看 20–54 岁人群的性别比例。AI 选址会根据业态偏好，拉取对应的周边信息，再结合交通条件和人口数据进行分析。 ### 2. 点位记录 选中点位后，可以快速加入记录，主要用来保存看中这个位置时的一些想法，以及实地考察时拍的照片。 ### 3. 选址评估 Agent 会根据内置的一些选址策略评估点位，最后通过绘图模型绘制一张直观的评估报告图。 ### 4. AI 能力 AI 助手在各个页面都可以调出，也能调用系统里的功能。整体希望往 AI Native 的方向发展一些。 目前内置了多种实体店类型的选址 Skill ，也接入了一个商业博主的商业分析 Skill ，可以一键使用。 这是一次把一些日常需求流快速用 ai 完成的尝试，整体使用 image2.5 做 ui 设计，gpt6.1-sol 做实现，后续会结合更多的软硬件+ai ，对实体比较有兴趣 下面是系统的一些图片： [![地图选址与人口热力图]( https://i.postimg.cc/05Xtyf1t/image.png)]( https://postimg.cc/yW9hf0d9) [![选址评估报告]( https://i.postimg.cc/pLWycDyF/image.png)]( https://postimg.cc/GHfcHTFL) [![AI 对话]( https://i.postimg.cc/C5CLm1gt/image.png)]( https://postimg.cc/8f5SCTsB)

projects.title: Show HN: Petal, open-source CoScreen/ScreenHero finally free
projects.author: thedracle
projects.summary: Hi HN! I’m Jason Thomas, one of the founders of CoScreen. As some of you may know, Datadog sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st. Four of us from the original CoScreen team have spent the last couple months building a free and open source pair programming tool inspired by those that came before us: It’s called Petal ( https://github.com/kiruna-labs/petal ) Some history first, because when we started CoScreen we had hoped to break the sad and established pattern of this industry. Screenhero was an exceptional tool that a lot of us loved for pairing. Multiple cursors, low latency, you could click your partner’s editor, and just start typing. It felt like magic while we had it. Then Slack bought it in 2015, and shut down the standalone app in December 2017. When Till, Max, and I started CoScreen, we were aware of this history, and wanted to build an even more magical collaboration and screen sharing experience: the entire concept was “throw a window from your laptop up on someone else’s screen, and start collaborating with zero friction.” Datadog acquired us in 2022, and thus began the great adventure of adapting our real-time technology into Datadog products, while also continue developing CoScreen as a standalone tool from the Datadog ecosystem. Datadog invested in the product for years and we’re thankful for that. But CoScreen itself proved, like so many other screen sharing tool acquisitions, to be too tangential from the customer base and core mission. We instead built other communication features in Datadog, the integrations with other video platforms, and also its wildly successful MCP server. We weren't the only ones. Around was bought by Miro and shut down in March 2025. Multi (formerly Remotion) was acqui-hired by OpenAI in 2024 and shut down about a month later. It's nearly always the same story: a small team builds something hard that people love, a platform buys it for the team or the feature, and the standalone product doesn't survive the integration. So we decided firmly to do things differently this time. Petal is completely free and open source and we aren't monetizing it. If we lose interest or get hit by a bus, you can self-host it or fork it, and nobody can sunset it on you. Honestly it's a love letter to everyone in this community that supported us, believed in us, and to liberate collaborative screen sharing from this vicious cycle. We hope through this we can help foster a large and vibrant community around innovating in this product sector. What Petal does: shared windows show up as real windows on your desktop, movable and resizable, not tiles in a grid. Several people can share at once, everyone gets a labeled cursor, and you can click into any shared window to type and scroll. Rooms are persistent, so you click once to join "eng-sync" instead of passing links around. It runs on macOS and Windows (Linux is next, this time for real and you can help us!), plus a web app. Media goes over LiveKit. You can use our hosted instance with zero config, or point the app at your own LiveKit server with one docker-compose if you want the traffic to stay on your network or even use an entirely different video backend if you want to. The part that still feels strange to us: CoScreen took almost six years to build. The first version of Petal took under eight weeks, from scratch, with frontier models like Fable and Astra doing a lot of the work. Real-time video and window capture is some of the most unforgiving code we have ever written, so we didn't expect that. We will do a proper writeup on what worked and what didn't, and are happy to answer questions about it here. Till, Darren, Max and I will be in the thread.

projects.title: Show HN: Working on Plug and play AI memory that works across AI agents
projects.author: heysrb
projects.summary: So I've been working on a project (Make0 AI) for a long time where I wanted to give common context to both Codex and Claude Code. The problem is simple - while working on Claude and after exhausting the daily/weekly limits I've start again from scratch in Codex. Of course I can prompt Claude to summarise a handoff that I can give to Codex but that is inefficient. So I thought of a creating a common context for both of them locally using a simple list of instructions like a shared md file. But the problem was the file kept on growing and after some point the common context went beyond 20k tokens and was just inflating the token budget unnecessarily. Then I implemented a RAG based retrieval approach on the list to only load what is required for that prompt and voila, after a few more iterations it resulted into a graph memory - Brain. So this product Make0 AI gives you the ability to create Brains that you can connect to any Ai agent via MCP and then they immediately know your likes, dislikes, preferences etc. AI agents can read, write to this memory. This can be your long term memory and the agents just become the token providers and task executors. You have full control over your data/memories from a single place. Think of this as a "USB thumb drive brain" that you plug to any agent. I know I may not be the first one to implement this but I tried to make the UX simple and is not at all developer focused. You can just drag and drop your memories/data to the brain and even play around with a visual brain. One more thing, i've done benchmarks on the memory. LoCoMo scores 83.3% overall, with Single hop 92.5% in standard mode (available now) and in another configuration (experimental max mode) it scores 92% overall and 94.4% in single hop. Available in the benchmark page. It uses hybrid search + graph memory and has built in conflict resolution for memories. Do let me know if you folks wanna try it!

github.name: Glittering/ai-browser
github.description: AI-native browser — renders pixels for humans, structured semantic tree API for agents. No screenshots, no OCR, no coordinate guessing.

projects.summary: npm： 官方 MCP Registry：io.github.Glittering/ai-browser AI Browser 是一个 Electron 浏览器，但"驾驶员"是 AI Agent：窗口正常可见、持久登录、常驻桌面，Agent 通过 17 个 MCP 工具（browse）或原始 WebSocket JSON-RPC 驱动它；遇到扫码、滑块、支付确认时，人随时可以接管鼠标，没有交接 API，也没有权限弹窗。 它和现有"截图 + OCR + 坐标"式 Agent 浏览器最大的区别是感知方式：Agent 拿到的是带 role/label/稳定元素 ID 的语义树（无障碍树基础上的结构化页面），不花视觉 token，也不怕页面位移。 点击与按键走 Chrome DevTools Protocol 受信输入（不是合成 JS 事件），Draft.js / ProseMirror / Quill / CKEditor 走同一条通道，无框架特判；点击后用 elementFromPoint 校验确实命中 browsediff 把"验证操作生效"做成工具原语：返回显式 changed/unchanged 判定、前后值与 JSON path，并对页面数据模型指纹化——ComfyUI 这类只改 canvas 数据、DOM 零变动的操作也能被识别 2D Canvas 文字在绘制层直接截获 fillText 字符串，无需 OCR；仅 WebGL 保留截图路径且默认关闭 Agent 后台操作时窗口不抢焦点（showInactive + 焦点模拟），并用 macOS lsappinfo 从外部做焦点测试 控制端口仅绑定 127.0.0.1；428 个单元测试（28 个文件）+ 428 个 Electron 端到端断言（12 个套件）全绿 已实测的真实网站流程：知乎文章发布（Draft.js 加粗/多段落/清空/发布弹层）、CSDN（CKEditor 正文/标签/摘要/发布）、百度与 Bing 搜索、东方财富（2458 语义节点）等。 安装：npx -y @glittering0717/ai-browser mcp（Node ≥ 18，已收录 MCP 官方 Registry，可直接被 Claude Code / Cursor / Codex 发现）。 利益关系说明：本人为项目作者，MIT 开源，无商业付费版本。当前已验证平台为 macOS 与 Linux，Windows 未测试，README 中如实标注；与 chrome-devtools-mcp、Playwright MCP 的定位差异也在 README 中做了对比说明。

projects.summary: Over the last 20 years, I repeatedly got frustrated with how slow WordPress (WP) is, especially once you stack a few plugins on it. Since 40% or what of all websites still run on WP, I decided [and please don't ask why, I have no idea what drove me] it could be useful to apply my C/C++ performance experience to a brand new from-scratch WP core to save about 50% of infrastructure while simultaneously increasing performance. With agent assisted coding I thought it could actually be doable to build out most of WP' API surface, and it was! (over multiple months) Try the live demo, including wp-admin! It shows WooCommerce + Elementor working, which is remarkable because I had to build an embeddable PHP runtime that covers most of Zend PHP's features for it. Runs 2x slower than Zend, but BookPress is still faster than a performance-tuned WP instance with OPCache, page cache and object caches. I don't mean to replace WP, and am faithfully implementing the API to avoid any divergence or "BookPress" handling in plugins or themes. BookPress is meant to run alongside a PHP WP installation, with a single-command migrate and un-migrate. Looking forward to what you all think.

projects.title: Show HN: Eevo – Consequential Decision Model
projects.author: ojalajuho
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Juho from Upright. I think we may have stumbled upon an interesting approach to AI alignment. The idea is as follows: 1. train a decision model to be really good at comparative sizing of consequences, expected value problems, and modelling overlap between different consequences 2. create a harness around that model that accepts a decision context, list of options, and identified consequences, then runs pairwise comparisons and overlap modelling for the consequences using the decision model in (1), and finally solves implied relative consequences "sizes" and finally EV (for different stakeholders) 3. Make AI agents running on general purpose LLMs use (2) to make better decisions. So the agent provides the context, options, and identifies the consequences, Eevo model just sizes them, models their overlap, and computes EV. In practice this seems to improve agent judgement a lot (in addition to adding lots of practical observability) It seems the (well-motivated) emphasis on instruction-following hurts model's performance on expected value tasks. The underlying decision model we trained beats Jev, Clef, MS decision-1 the model on OpenAI decisions API on economic rationality benchmarks like STEEP, expected value tasks, poker, and even Pacman (Jevman benchmark). I swear to you we did not Benchmaxx on Pacman Also it seems to be useful also for human decisions. Just getting other people's decisions presented to you in standard format with consequences listed and sized is just very pleasant. There are some testers though who think this is useful for improving everyone's judgement, except their own

github.description: 把行情放在菜单栏，随时掌握市场动态。macOS 菜单栏 / Windows 悬浮行情条的 A 股盯盘小工具：实时价格、涨跌幅、分时图抬眼就能看，不占 Dock。Tauri 2 + 原生 TypeScript

projects.summary: 项目：StockBar | 平台：macOS / Windows / Linux | 许可：MIT | 最新版本：v0.0.6 它是什么 一个把行情放进菜单栏的开源盯盘小工具，Tauri 2 + Rust + 原生 TypeScript。 盘中想瞄一眼自选，又不想一直开着完整的行情软件 —— 那类软件占地方、还显眼。StockBar 把常看的几只留在菜单栏，点一下展开指数、自选和分时图，看完就收起。macOS 上不占 Dock；Windows 托盘放不下文字，就另外给一条可拖动的悬浮行情条。 界面是真的轻：不用 UI 框架、不用图表库，列表是原生 DOM 拼的，分时图是 canvas 一笔一笔画的。数据走东方财富的公开接口，失败时自动切到腾讯，所以不用注册、不用 API Key。 功能详解 📌 抬眼就能看见 菜单栏常驻，最多放 3 个标的。三种样式：单行文字、双行紧凑、仅图标 —— 双行是 canvas 按 2x 绘制的 PNG，两张一行摆得下名称、价格和涨跌幅。名称、价格、涨跌幅可以各自开关，顺序也能拖。 📊 分时图与成交额 点指数卡片或自选行就展开当天的分时，再点一次收起。内置上证、深证成指、创业板指；大盘指数的分时多取一天，用来算「与上一日同期」的成交额对比，个股则是单日。 🗂️ 自选与分组 搜索支持代码、名称和拼音；置顶、拖动排序、自定义分组都在。分组多了筛选条会横向滑动，末尾的 ☰ 把全部分组摊成一片标签，带每组的自选数量，点一下就切过去。加入菜单栏、移入分组、删除都支持批量。 菜单栏常驻，最多放 3 个标的。三种样式：单行文字、双行紧凑、仅图标 —— 双行是 canvas 按 2x 绘制的 PNG，两行摆得下名称、价格和涨跌幅。名称、价格、涨跌幅可以各自开关，顺序也能拖。 自带零依赖的 MCP 服务（11 个工具），支持 MCP 的 AI 客户端可以按你的话操作： 「新建一个『持仓』分组，把宁德时代加进去并置顶。」 「把苹果和英伟达移到『观察』分组。」 命令通过本机 127.0.0.1 上的随机端口交给应用执行，走的是和手点界面完全相同的校验与同步规则，界面会立刻跟着变。这一步默认关闭，需要时到设置里拨开。 ⚙️ 按自己的习惯来 跟随系统 / 浅色 / 深色主题，红涨绿跌 / 绿涨红跌，3 / 5 / 10 / 30 秒刷新，报价与分时可固定用东方财富或腾讯。安装后能在「关于」页检查更新、一键升级。 两个平台各长什么样 macOS 是自绘窗口控件的菜单栏小窗（360×560），Windows 走平台布局：托盘 + 桌面悬浮行情条，托盘图标随任务栏深浅自动着色。 技术栈 | 部分 | 选型 | | --- | --- | | 桌面外壳 | Tauri 2、Rust | | 界面 | 原生 TypeScript、Vite、canvas（无 UI 框架、无图表库） | | 数据 | 东方财富公开接口，失败时自动切腾讯 | | MCP | 零依赖 stdio JSON-RPC 服务 + Rust 侧本地 HTTP 桥 | | 测试 | Vitest（前端纯逻辑 + MCP 脚本，含一条起进程的端到端用例） | 快速开始 macOS 与 Windows 都有现成安装包（Linux 暂无官方预编译包，可从源码运行）： 下载： 从源码跑，需要 Node.js 22+、pnpm、Rust stable 和对应平台的 Tauri 2 开发依赖： bash git clone cd stock-bar pnpm install pnpm app:dev 只想看界面的话 pnpm dev 即可，浏览器里 Tauri 调用会降级为空操作。 需要说清楚的几件事 macOS 安装包暂未签名与公证，首次打开请右键「打开」，或 xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StockBar.app。 交易状态按市场时区和报价里的最后成交时间推断，没有节假日日历，开盘前无法提前判定当天是否休市。 行情来自公开接口，刷新频率不代表交易所级实时性；覆盖范围以数据源返回为准。 项目还很年轻（v0.0.6），用着顺手或者踩到坑，都欢迎来 Issues 说一声。觉得有用的话，点一颗 Star 就是最大的鼓励 ⭐️

projects.title: Show HN: Run AI-generated logic safely inside your app
projects.author: cj-builds
projects.summary: Stof is an open-source runtime for logic you don't own or fully trust. Imagine a JSON document with functions inside, scoped to just the document that contains them. Stof instantiates this doc as a small wasm env, and makes these functions safe to call. They can't access or manipulate anything but their own doc. WebAssembly by itself is large in binary form, requires a lot of tooling, etc. Stof can be sent over the wire easily, is a superset of JSON for compatibility, and keeps the guarantees. I created Stof not to replace a data format or anything, but to be a glue layer for data and distributed systems to work with one another. This includes I/O for interchange data like JSON, YAML, TOML, etc., but also complex data like PDFs, images, binaries, both structured and unstructured (good layer to turn one into the other). The fact is, the layer of data and communication between apps tends to be a bit messy, and strict adapters compiled at build time tend to be insufficient for the dynamism of modern software. This applies directly to AI-generated data and code, which is basically like calling into another untrusted service. With this, you can safely embed the execution, pick where things run, and combine harnesses like data. Works well as a "living" context, also with the JSON interop - just parse into or stringify sections of the Stof doc at runtime when needed, like agent tool defs. The playground on the site runs entirely in your browser. Stof is written in Rust and has support for JS/TS and Python today. I'd especially like feedback on whether the idea makes sense from the landing page, and where the docs need help. GitHub: https://github.com/dev-formata-io/stof Thank you!! -CJ

projects.summary: Grove 是一个 macOS 菜单栏应用加命令行工具，面向拆分在多个 Git 仓库里的项目（比如客户端、服务端、配置各在一个仓库）。它为每个功能建一个“工作区”：一个目录里放着你选的各个仓库的 git worktree，都在同一个分支上。Claude Code 从这个目录启动，看到的是这几个仓库的同一个分支；同时开好几个会话，也不会互相把分支切走。它还能集中查看各项目、各账号的 Claude Code 会话，并把会话转到另一个 Claude 账号继续。 亮点 一个分支贯穿多个仓库：建工作区时，Grove 在你选的每个仓库里执行 git worktree add，分支名按模板生成（默认 feat/{name}），你指定的共享文件（比如 CLAUDE.md）会链接或复制进新工作区，各仓库还可以运行自己的创建后钩子。每个仓库可以从各自的基础分支开始；新工作区也能基于另一个工作区的分支来建，Grove 直接从 git 推导出它们之间的关系。 和 Claude Code 自带的 --worktree 不同：claude --worktree 只在当前这一个仓库里建 worktree，Grove 把多个仓库的 worktree 放在同一个目录、同一个分支上。如果产品只有一个仓库，Claude Code 自带的功能可能就够用了。 会话集中查看，还能换账号：列出各个项目、各个 Claude 账号下的 Claude Code 会话。一个账号的限额用完时，可以把会话交给另一个账号：Resume as… 用另一个账号直接接着跑，什么都不用复制；Migrate to… 把会话记录、记忆、文件历史和任务完整复制过去；Share 把会话放进共享存储，所有关联的账号都能看到。 另外还有提交图（分支、远程、标签）和代码行数统计；命令行工具 grove 提供 scan、workspaces、sessions、create、graph、doctor 命令，都能输出 JSON。 可以当学习材料：怎样为多个仓库批量创建 git worktree，并确认它们都切到了同一个分支；菜单栏为什么用 NSStatusItem + NSPanel，而不用 SwiftUI 的 MenuBarExtra，也不用 NSPopover（GroveMenuBarApp.swift 的注释里写了原因）。 纯 Swift 编写（SwiftUI + AppKit），没有第三方依赖，有九百多个测试；免费，GPL-3.0 开源；仓库附有简体中文 README。

projects.title: Show HN: T0: We trained a 256M SOTA open-weights time-series forecasting model
projects.author: LTMeyer

github.name: theforecastingcompany/tfc-t0
github.description: An open-weights time-series forecasting foundation model from The Forecasting Company.

projects.summary: Hi everyone, we are excited to share t0-gamma, the latest model in our t0 family. It is a 256M parameter open-weights foundation model for time series (TSFM). It runs on CPU, GPU or Apple chips. https://huggingface.co/theforecastingcompany/t0-gamma t0 leverages historical data to forecast the likely outcomes over a given horizon. It does so zero-shot. It works on almost any time series, as it can pick up small signals like trends and seasonality. It can also leverage future-known information, like holidays, promotions and weather forecasts. Under the hood, t0 is a transformer that alternates attention between time and across the variates of a series. t0 is agnostic to the domain and to the frequency of the time series. For instance, it can be used to predict retail or electricity demand, as well as server metrics. On European day ahead electricity prices, t0 reduces the error by a third compared with a naive baseline that repeats the previous day. Adding weather forecasts or holiday information improves it even further. There is a Colab notebook to try it. t0 has also been tested independently on electricity prices in Texas (ERCOT). https://colab.research.google.com/github/theforecastingcompa... Like other TSFMs, t0 outperforms classical techniques such as ARIMA, ETS and their variants. On the public benchmarks GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME, t0-gamma currently ranks first among the other TSFMs. It means it is the most accurate model there is to date. Like other TSFMs, t0 can be used inside agentic, routing or ensembling systems. This can improve the scores on the leaderboards even further. Our tech report describes the model family and its evaluation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24559 Trying it takes a few Python lines. pip install "tfc-t0[torch]>=0.6.0" from t0 import T0Forecaster model = T0Forecaster.from_pretrained("theforecastingcompany/t0-gamma").eval() history = ... # history of the time series to predict out = model.predict(history, horizon=24) out.median There is more to come. We are working to extend t0 to joint forecasts across related series and hierarchies, much longer contexts and faster inference. Please give it a try, and don't hesitate to tell us where it works and where it doesn't. We are The Forecasting Company. We want to help companies reduce their uncertainty about the future, so they can make better decisions. We are starting our journey by building foundation models for time series.

projects.title: Show HN: tsv has fast formatters and parsers for Svelte, TypeScript/JS, CSS
projects.author: ryanatkn
projects.summary: tsv is a set of performance-focused language tools for the Web. Today it ships formatters and parsers for TypeScript/JS, CSS, and Svelte, including a vscode/openvsx extension. JSON and HTML are planned, maybe linting after. The readme has a loose roadmap - https://github.com/fuzdev/tsv tsv's benchmarks show how the Web's newer native tools have some performance left on the table. Formatting TypeScript, tsv is more than twice as fast as oxfmt, and is smaller and uses less memory - https://tsv.fuz.dev/docs/benchmarks From the site: - formatting TypeScript, tsv is ~2.2x faster than Oxfmt (native), ~36x faster than Prettier (native Rust vs Prettier's JS; ~26x as wasm), and ~7.6x faster than Biome (wasm) - formatting Svelte, tsv is ~79x faster than Prettier (~55x as wasm) and ~10x faster than Biome (wasm) - formatting CSS, tsv is ~3.6x faster than Oxfmt (native), ~111x faster than Prettier (~78x as wasm), and ~12x faster than Biome (wasm) tsv is focused on the Web and Svelte, and doesn't support other nonstandard languages like JSX/TSX and SCSS. This limits possible adoption, but it keeps the tool slim and simple, and there are plenty of other tools that offer a generic language platform - tsv isn't trying to compete with them. Part of my motivation was being tired of slow tools and Svelte's second-class status in this next generation. Before starting the project, I had tried to build on Oxc and Biome, and ran into some discouraging edges. On the benchmarks' language support section, you'll see Oxc doesn't export its CSS parser (recently added, a fork of Raffia - https://github.com/g-plane/raffia ), and Biome doesn't export its parsers. Also oxfmt doesn't ship wasm to the browser yet, and tsv's smaller footprint is useful there (Biome is 46.9 MB to tsv's 2.7). Parser conformance is as good or better than Oxc, Biome, and swc, except negative parser cases (errors), which are unfinished. https://tsv.fuz.dev/docs/conformance The codebase turns 1 year old at the end of the month. It's my first serious AI-generated project, built with Claude Code. I learned Rust in 2015, built some toys including an arcade action prototype, and followed its development over the years, but this is my first project since. tsv wouldn't exist without LLMs - it requires far too much labor for a side project. tsv leans heavily on Prettier, but doesn't copy it. This is why this production release took almost a year, despite the silly fast coding part. I made some different stylistic choices, more for Svelte than TypeScript, and fixed numerous quirks and bugs and documented them. tsv also takes advantage of Svelte 5's whitespace rules, which further diverged from HTML to trim leading whitespace in tags, fixing longstanding formatting warts - https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide#Whitespace... The formatter takes no style config, and instead is hardcoded to Prettier's style with Svelte's config. Supporting Prettier's config would force significant costs on tsv with a JS runtime, so instead I'm keeping the formatters non-configurable instead of making all users pay those costs. Part of these costs can be see in the CLI benchmark (which is a fork of Oxc's official bench-formatter) - when tsv's binary is used directly instead of via Node, the single-repo CLI benchmark runs tsv 1.7x faster using less than half the memory. Next I'm exploring rearchitecting to Zig-inspired data-oriented parsing - https://mitchellh.com/zig/parser - which should get tsv closer to Yuku's speed, measured on the site. The vscode extension is `fuzdev.tsv-format` - https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=fuzdev.t... - and Open VSX - https://open-vsx.org/extension/fuzdev/tsv-format Repo: https://github.com/fuzdev/tsv

projects.title: 【开源自荐】MastraWork：把 Agent 运行组织成任务的开源桌面 AI 工作台
projects.author: movclantian

github.name: movclantian/mastra-desktop
github.description: Local-first multi-agent coding workbench built on Electron, React and the Mastra framework. 本地优先的开源桌面 AI 工作台，基于 Mastra + Electron，把一次 Agent 运行组织成可暂停、可回溯、可交接的任务。

projects.summary: 项目：MastraWork | 平台：Windows / macOS / Linux | 许可：Apache-2.0 | 最新版本：v0.0.7 它是什么 一个本地优先的开源桌面 AI 工作台，底层是 Mastra 框架 + Electron。 它想解决的事情很具体：现在多数 AI 工具给你一段回答，事情就停在那儿；代码改到一半让它继续，它常常重新把文件读一遍，从接不上的地方往下编。前面聊过的上下文，像是没发生过。 MastraWork 的做法是把一次 Agent 运行组织成一个任务。任务落在具体的工作区里，长在线程上，每一步都留下痕迹。它能暂停，能回头检查，也能交给团队里的其他成员接着看。断掉之后不是从头再来，而是接着往下走。 它面向软件工程和知识工作：Agent、团队、工作区、终端、浏览器、MCP、技能和资料库收在同一个应用里，围着同一个任务转。 功能详解 🧭 工程任务 读取代码、全局搜索、编辑与 AST 修改、运行命令、查看差异、调用 LSP 都在里面。关键是读、写、执行分开授权，每一步都有记录，不是开一个大权限就全放开。 🛡️ 受控执行 计划、构建、复查三种模式，切的是「Agent 现在能碰什么」。人工询问和批准留在流程里，高风险动作停下来等人确认，不靠模型自觉。 👥 Agent 团队 主 Agent 可以带一群专家成员，支持委派、交接、并行、分支、循环和审批工作流。复杂任务拆给合适的人，而不是一个 Agent 硬扛。 🧩 开放扩展 模型 Provider、MCP Server、技能与插件、浏览器、资料库、记忆和网页检索，按需接入，不绑定任何一家模型服务。今天用这家，明天想换，配置改一下就行。 🖥️ 桌面集成 Electron 主进程、原生浏览器视图、PTY 终端、系统通知、凭据保险库。API Key、OAuth token 和 Cookie 由桌面主进程的凭据保险库保管。 📚 记忆与资料库 记忆跨会话保留；资料库统一收文档、表格和网页；用量、费用和历史数据随时可查。 一个任务是怎么走完的 一个任务从开工到验收，Agent 手里的权限是变的，分三个阶段： 1. 计划 —— 先把事情想清楚，读代码、查资料、出方案。 2. 构建 —— 方案定了再动手，改代码、跑命令、推进任务，每一步都留下记录，随时可以停下来回头看。 3. 复查 —— 对照差异和工作记录验收，高风险的操作在这一步需要人批准。 读、编辑、执行和外部工具在三阶段各有一套策略，图的入口在应用内设置里，实际安全性以服务端权限检查和测试记录为准。 技术栈 | 部分 | 选型 | | --- | --- | | 桌面外壳 | Electron 44、electron-vite、electron-builder | | 界面 | React 19、TypeScript、Tailwind CSS 4、CodeMirror 6、xterm | | Agent 框架 | Mastra 1.77（core、memory、rag、mcp、observability） | | 数据与检索 | libsql、DuckDB、fastembed 本地向量 | | 代码与文档 | Shiki 高亮、Mermaid、KaTeX、PDF 与 Office 解析 | | 工具链 | Biome、Knip、pnpm workspace | 快速开始 三个平台都有现成安装包，也可以从源码跑（需要 Node.js >=22.19.0 <23、pnpm 12.11.2）： sh corepack enable corepack prepare pnpm@12.11.2 --activate pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm dev 首次启动后配一个可用的模型 Provider、选一个工作区目录即可。需要网页检索、浏览器、MCP 或技能时，再按实际服务分别配置凭据。默认本地数据目录是 ~/.mastrawork，Mastra 服务跑在本机 4111 端口。 下载： 关于「本地优先」 需要说清楚一点：「本地优先」说的是桌面宿主、默认工作区和本地数据边界优先留在本机，不表示所有推理都在本地完成。模型推理走哪个服务由使用者自己配置，模型服务会收到你发过去的提示词和选定的上下文。 项目还在很早期（v0.0.7），用着顺手或者踩到坑，都欢迎来 Issues 说一声。

projects.title: Show HN: Factory DS, A Factorio-Like Game for the Nintendo DS
projects.author: j_leboulanger
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Ronan. I love the Nintendo DS but ran out of games that kept me hooked, so I tried porting the kind of game I play today: a factory game in the spirit of Factorio, on a 67 MHz ARM9 with 4 MB of RAM. I had never written code for the DS, and I built it with Claude Code. I wrote the specs, the design and the balancing, and Claude wrote most of the C. The post goes through how that worked, and through the technical parts I found the most fun: - a 2048x2048 world that is never stored: terrain is computed from (x, y), only the player's changes are kept in a hash table - night done by changing the 256-color palette instead of redrawing the screen - power grids and pipes computed per network with union-find (there is a small step-by-step animation in the post) - trains with schedules, block signals and pathfinding, plus redstone-like logic gates - a headless Mac build of the game with a text interface, so AI agents could play ~470 test sessions and even help balance the game You can download the ROM (English and French) and play it on a flashcart or in melonDS.

projects.title: Show HN: Hatoba, an open-source SSH client with an AI assistant and E2EE sync
projects.author: scarletkc

github.name: scarletkc/Hatoba
github.description: Open-source desktop SSH client with an AI assistant and end-to-end encrypted sync through your own Cloudflare account

projects.summary: I've used SSH tools for years and didn't really plan on building yet another SSH client, but I ended up building one the way I wanted. Hatoba is a desktop SSH client for Windows, Linux and macOS. It's written in Rust with Tauri 2 and MIT licensed. Each terminal has an AI assistant panel next to it. You describe the problem, and it reads the terminal screen, runs commands, types into the shell, and reads, edits and searches files on the host to find the cause and fix it. You can approve every command and edit it before it runs, let a model you pick approve the safe ones, or turn approval off. Files it changes show a diff you can undo. It works with any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic API, local models included, and supports skills and MCP servers. Sync doesn't go through a server of mine. Hatoba deploys a Worker and a D1 database to your own Cloudflare account and syncs hosts, keys and AI conversations through them. The free plan usually covers personal use. Everything is encrypted on the device before it leaves. Keys are derived from your master password with Argon2id, every item is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the Worker only stores ciphertext plus the hashes it needs to sign you in. Someone who gets hold of the whole Cloudflare account still only gets ciphertext. Sync is optional, and everything works offline without it. The usual SSH client features are there too: groups, tags and fuzzy search, ~/.ssh/config import, ProxyJump and SOCKS5/HTTP proxies, an SFTP panel, local port forwarding, and a key vault that imports OpenSSH, PEM and PuTTY keys. There's also a dashboard showing CPU, memory, disk and network for every saved host, read over plain SSH with nothing installed on the servers. SSH is russh, the terminal is xterm.js with the WebGL renderer, and the UI is React. I develop on Windows, so it's Windows first, with a custom title bar that supports Snap Layouts and Mica, and working CJK input methods. The Linux packages and the macOS build get far less testing on real machines. The macOS build is Apple Silicon only and isn't notarized, so macOS blocks it on first launch until you allow it in Privacy & Security. Bug reports from Linux and Mac users would help the most. Website: https://hatoba.fog.moe Downloads: https://hatoba.fog.moe/download/

projects.title: Show HN: Merlin, Run Your Claude Code and Codex from Slack, Linear and GitHub
projects.author: dottchen
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Merlin to let you use your own Claude Code and Codex subscription from Slack, Linear, and GitHub. There is a desktop app for macOS and Windows, and a CLI daemon for Linux. When someone mentions Merlin in a Slack thread or Linear issue comment, the task runs on that team member's machine, using their own Claude Code or Codex runtime, and progress and results come back to the original thread. Teammates can steer the agent mid-run. Merlin also has schedules, shared skills, and memory. I know you've probably heard about Claude Tag. Merlin is similar to that but also different. The model usage goes to the Claude Code or Codex subscription instead of API bill, and you can use Merlin across different surfaces to streamline workflow instead of just in Slack (Linear's agent session works particularly well with Merlin. You can just leverage Linear as your control panel for agentic work using Merlin). Merlin also runs on your local machines, which means that you can use your local context including MCPs, skills and local files instead of in a cloud sandbox. Merlin does not upload your working directory, and provider credentials stay on the device. The request and the context it needs pass through Merlin. Runtimes start private, and an owner can make one public so teammates, including non-engineers, can use it. But there're also some limits, and we'll probably deal with them in future updates: - An offline or sleeping machine can't take work. The same issue as OpenClaw. But if you have a mac mini or ec2 setup it should be fine. - Linux is CLI only. We may later add desktop for Linux. - While runtime delegation isn't a problem for now, we're still working on how to make the best use of each team member's local runtime and let them work together cohesively. We've been internally using Merlin for quite some time. It really helps when you're trying to add some AI juice to the conversation or just delegate things to your agents. I think it reduces the friction of having to do the copying & pasting and switch to another app to ask for AI's input when you're having a discussion in a collaborative environment like Slack or Linear. It's really the fastest way from intent to execution. Pricing: free for up to 5 active users and 1,000 requests/month. We think this should get small teams started and get real value from it. Team is $59/mo and Scale is $99/mo, with a 14-day Team trial and no credit card required. I'm here all day to answer questions, and I'd especially like to hear whether non-engineers on your team would actually use this.

projects.title: Show HN: Ret – An inbox and canvas for your Codex and Claude Code agents
projects.author: itsjustmechris
projects.summary: Over the last few weeks I've really been using Codex and Claude to solve a lot of parallel tasks, across a lot of different projects. This lead me to wishing that I could interface with my agents in the same way that I interface with my already existing windows and editors. For me, this usually means that I have like 5 to anywhere around 8 different windows that I drag around depending on where I want to focus, this could mean I am focusing on the terminal now, or I want to test stuff in a simulator or browser; but when I go to interface with agents, I have to manage many tabs, or I have to look through a list in their native apps. This is not convenient for me, and I'm almost certain this is not convenient for many of you. That's why I built an infinite canvas, where my traditional desktop style workflow can come to life alongside my agents, I can drag them around depending on where I want my focus to be, or I can let them just pile up, like the 15 finder windows you're hiding with your browser right now. But, when I do want to go back to that thread, I will intuitively just know right where it is. I didn't stop there though, I really enjoyed the inbox style agent interface that Google shipped many months ago with Anti Gravity, but I didn't really enjoy much other than that, so, I built that in too. But, I still didn't stop there, a traditional code editor still comes in handy every once and awhile, just to read, or to tradcode, though Ret doesn't feature a VS-Code fork, yet anyways, maybe one day something similar could exist, it does feature a fairly comparable implementation, powered by the same technology, in a similar layout, just without the plugins and bloat. But, I didn't stop there either, the traditional sidebar and one centered chat is a nice experience sometimes, so I built that in too. I guess you probably can see where this is going, but that's also not where I stopped. Working on a single focused thread can be beneficial, but I am a heavy fork user, so I made it convenient to work side by side your main thread and a fork, with ambitions to expand on this in the future as I feel out how many forks or side chats are worth working on at the same time in the 'focused' view. But focus view doesn't stop there, instead of having only one chat in focus, and having to then jump back to the sidebar, I thought, well hey, browser tabs are great, so I built those in too. I know it sounds like there's a lot of things built in here, and there is, but trust me, it doesn't feel bloated at all, it feels amazing. I really think this is something that greatly benefits my productivity, and I hope that some of you also feel my excitement when trying it out.

projects.title: [开源推荐] MCDIndex —— 全国城市麦当劳指数
projects.author: wengshirui

github.name: wengshirui/mcdindex
github.description: 横向比较不同城市的麦当劳门店供给数量

projects.summary: 用麦当劳官方 MCP 扫了全国 337 个地级及以上行政区的 5,817 家门店，算出一个 0~100 的城市麦当劳指数。输入城市名或地址关键词，就能看到这座城市在同级城市中的排名，以及门店密度、核心区覆盖、得来速占比三个分项。项目含纯函数计算引擎、离线数据快照与自包含演示页，打开即用、不联网。 亮点 把接口限制变成产品定义，而不是硬刚：MCP 的门店接口单次固定只返回 5 家、无分页、经纬度恒为 0.0，拿不到门店总数。项目用同构关键词采样（城市名 + 区县 + 通用道路 + 通用 POI）绕开上限，并把产品语义直接定义成「只做同级别比较」，同时在页面明写拿到的是采样下界。 一道「防假精度」护栏：给近乎无差异的指标算百分位，等于把噪声放大成排名差异。实测全国 117 个共有 SKU 的挂牌价篮子相对极差只有 0.285，低于设定的 0.30 阈值，于是价格维度被降级为「只展示、不计分」。 用公开数据反向校验自己：把采样门店数逐省与公开门店数对照，量化覆盖率，并写清偏差方向 —— 门店越密的城市越容易被低估（南京实测覆盖率仅约 59%）。 工程上可直接取用：计算引擎是纯函数、零 I/O 零第三方依赖；71 项三态自测（通过 / 失败 / 跳过，「跳过」不算通过）；演示页是单文件，打开即用，不联网也不调 MCP。

projects.title: Show HN: Helicon – Desktop App for Meta's Muse Code CLI (Linux, Windows, macOS)
projects.author: harjjotsinghh
projects.summary: Hi Hacker News, I'm Harjot. I've been using Meta's Muse Code CLI daily for a few weeks now. One thing that I found difficult to handle was managing or controlling multiple sessions across multiple projects, while using the terminal for the muse CLI. Initially, I used cmux to create workspaces/groups for my different projects to group them, and then created 4 split terminals in each of those projects, that ran muse code sessions in each of them. It worked, but it was ugly. I didn't like using that. It could be because I'm not really a terminal person and would much rather prefer a proper dedicated GUI or desktop/app interface, and I would prefer it any time over a terminal screen or CLI. So it might be personal preference but yeah. So, I started building a desktop app around it, mainly to scratch my own itch. Helicon is a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, plus a VS Code extension that also works in Cursor and Devin. It doesn't replace the CLI. It runs `muse serve` and talks to it, and it reuses your existing `muse login`, so you don't have to get an API key and you don't pay an extra bill. You can use your existing Muse Code subscription plans. Some things that I use the most: 1. Resuming sessions that I started in the terminal. I don't start many sessions in the terminal now that Helicon exists, but initially I wanted to access all the sessions that were running in a terminal to be accessible from Helicon, when it was created initially. 2. Inline diffs that I can approve, similar to how Cursor works. 3. I can clearly see my 5-hour and weekly plan limits directly from the app itself and don't have to manually keep going to Meta's Muse Code billing page and manually keep refreshing the page to see my current usage/limits. I built it using Tauri 2 and React. It is MIT licensed. I built a lot of it with AI coding agents, especially Opus 5.5 (I really like using this model). It's at v0.21.9 now, and 9 people have contributed so far. Some issues: the Windows installer isn't code-signed yet, so you'll see a SmartScreen warning. And the macOS build isn't notarized, so you need to click "Open Anyway" once. You can try it in the browser with mock data, no install needed: https://helicon.sh/try It's unofficial and not affiliated with Meta. If you use a coding CLI every day, what would you want from a GUI for it? And what would make you go back to the terminal?

projects.title: Show HN: Laya guard – a local check before your coding agent runs a command
projects.author: ayaan0209
projects.summary: HN, this is my first Show HN post, and I'm really nervous, I'm Ayaan, a Frontend Developer. laya-guard is a local check that occurs before any coding agent tool call, deciding whether to approve, send for review, or block the call. When Jev was released, I was curious as to how I could use it, and I quickly discovered Laya which is an open-source 322M model that functions almost identically but runs on a laptop's CPU in under 100ms, as the check is local, there won't be a chance of 3rd parties seeing your commands, directories, or tokens, and there's no charge per call, I often work in Korean, and most of the guardrails I've seen have not evaluated Korean at all, hence why I've implemented it as well. Regex policies catch known dangerous patterns before even reaching models, any command that is blocked is never seen by models, commands like ls, git status, and npm test will skip the model altogether, unless they have pipes, chaining, redirects, -exec flags, or sensitive paths, everything else is sent to the model for processing, once you have the model downloaded, it makes decisions from a fixed set of outcomes with no API key or request needed for any external service, there are also hooks for 11 different agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and many more. And Also a local dashboard where you can see all decision and why it was made and install the hook for each agent, it doesn't save the commands themeslves. In my tests with AgentDojo, it blocked 25/27 attacks, and allowed 92/97 harmless tasks, it correctly identified 64/66 commands I made. After the Reddit post, people have found some issues with it: Adding a comment at the end of a command would fool the model to not block the command. The model only read the first 4,000 characters, so it could be spammed with junk to the beginning to bypass the check, this would send dangerous commands like curl to review. "curl" repeated 40,000 times caused one regex to run for 48 seconds, timing out the hook and running the command. All 3 issues have already been fixed, somebody also pointed out that if the server was down, commands ran without any check, now it asks you first, or blocks the command if the agent can't ask Please note that this is not a tool to check if the code written is correct, it's a tool to prevent agents from running dangerous commands.

projects.title: Show HN: Enso Method – agent skills for building software for someone else
projects.author: dwkerwin
projects.summary: The Enso Method is a new set of AI skills for Claude Code and Codex which I've open sourced on GitHub predominantly for developers who build for someone else who is making the product/business calls. I've been using AI to write basically 100% of my code since late 2024, back in the Sonnet 3.5 days, when it barely worked and there were few people doing this and very little support for this way of developing. I stubbornly thought this was going to be the future and came up with a methodology for making it work, before "AI skills" were even a thing. Since then I've continued to refine the method and I just recently published it as open source. The method focuses on requirements (PRD, TDD) up front, and has skills that autonomously refine the requirements, declaring assumptions that should be validated by stakeholders. It doesn't expect you to be a solo founder or that whoever is at the keyboard directing Claude or Codex to be the product owner and business decider in addition to being the developer. I think most of us sit in the seat where we develop for someone else who decides. And if AI is all about velocity, then if we have to slow down to get product owners to review and decide, that puts a serious damper on the efficiency everyone expects from AI development. So a defining attribute of the Enso Method is, when it reviews the requirements prior to implementation, it asks what questions/gaps there are and it tries to answer its own questions. If it can get to 95%+ confidence in the answers, it just rolls with those. If less then it will declare the assumption in an assumptions.md file which gets routed to business stakeholders to review. In the meantime however we still consider this to be a green light, we can move forward and implement with the assumptions, and if we later hear from the business that the assumption was wrong, we update the requirements and re-implement, because implementation is now cheap, and waiting isn't.

projects.author: zw-onemaker-ai

github.description: 🏭 AI 工程化交付系统 — 把完整工程团队的工序编进一条多 Agent 管线：14 角色 · 三道验证闸门 · EXIT_CODE 指纹 · 定向回环 · 三层记忆。实战产出：AgentGate（127 项测试）。

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个开源项目： 一句话：把完整工程团队的 14 个角色和工序，编成一条多 Agent 的交付管线。我不缺会用 AI 写代码的工具，缺的是「工序」——谁先谁后、什么算完成、出错了往哪退。这三个问题不解决，交付质量就只能靠运气。 这个项目的思路是把「制度」做进管线：每个角色的产出必须过三道闸门才能交给下一个角色（① 文件真实存在且非空 ② 所有验证命令必须贴出 EXITCODE——Agent 编得了话，编不了退出码 ③ 面向用户的产出过脱敏检查）；审查不通过不盲目重跑，而是按问题类型回环到对应角色；三层记忆给上下文装硬上限，防膨胀。 几个我觉得有意思的点：它不是新的 Agent 框架，而是「跑在 Agent 之上的制度」——一份可直接被 Claude Code 等编程 Agent 使用的协议集；零第三方依赖，仓库里 3 个 Demo（门禁 / 记忆 / 管线漫游）clone 下来 1 分钟跑完；最近还给它加了 RSI 自我迭代——失误登记 → 预防闸门 → 自动验证，管线会自己修自己的流程。 这是继 AgentGate（管线可靠性层）后的第二条线：一个管「点」（每个产出可不可信），这个管「面」（整条交付线有没有工序），可以配合使用。MIT 协议，欢迎拍砖。

projects.title: Show HN: shadowclone, skills learned from your coding agent corrections
projects.author: theonly1me
projects.summary: shadowclone reads the coding-agent sessions already on your disk, finds where you corrected the agent and turns those corrections into skills your agents load next time. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and Antigravity. Every capture source is off by default and has its own consent setting. Why I'm building it? I use multiple harnesses and agents, I extensively use Claud Code and Codex, but I also use Cursor and Antigravity every now and then. I didn't want to have to teach every harness or model the things I taught the other ones between my last session and the current one. I also cannot have my personal rules and preferences in all the repositories I work on because my collaborators may have varying levels of trust with AI and their own preferences. shadowclone helps me build and improve trust with my agents so I can give them more autonomy while running multiple sessions in parallel. --- Who is this for? If you only use Claude or Codex or any one of these, you may not need the shadowclone CLI and the harness and agent you use might already be sufficient. But, if you are like me and work across harnesses and agents, shadowclone will help you avoid repeating your preferences each time. --- Built-in skills and skill builds shadowclone is also great for someone who is just now adopting AI into their coding workflows because it ships with several skills that they can use to customize their agent's behavior. They can equip all the skills, or just some of them, they'll see the "personality" their agent gets from equipping those skills from the `shadowclone wizard`. --- Setup is extremely easy, just ask your Claude Code, or Codex, or another agent - "Set up shadowclone: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/mai... " --- Privacy shadowclone is free and open source, it uses the MIT license. It doesn't have a subscription, or a server. It just uses your existing agent subscription i.e. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or even your local model via Pi. You can explicitly disable sources, it also redacts any and all sensitive information it uses for learning. --- PR reviews and Cloud bots It can review PRs with the `shadowclone review` command, it ships a guided review skill that will perform a deep review of your code (or someone else's) and produce an HTML document you can annotate, add comments to and submit so your agent can stage a draft review on the PR you are reviewing. --- Evals I performed several evals, I won't describe them here, all of them are available in the repository - https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main/evals --- Comparison to other tools? You can also see how it compares to other tools here - https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main#how-shad...

projects.title: Show HN: Hapsland – Realtime semantic advice on coding standards for the agents
projects.author: Firfi
projects.summary: Agents ignore AGENTS.md mid-session. Then you tell them: hey, this is written in AGENTS.md. - "You're absolutely right!" (proceeds with fixing) But not anymore! This is a tool that would check the code immediately with a classifier (Jev etc.) and give the agent advice in the same turn. It catches some mistakes that are difficult to put into lint rules and excels at the cases when semantic understanding is required - e.g. field names/types in a nested structure that contradict each other (more commonly known as "invalid states") (that we strive to make, e.g. "unrepresentable", some would say) Even reviewer agent loops won't do much (as Primeagen's X post a month ago shows in all the colours [which I don't know if I can or can not link, and will stay on the safe side of not doing so]). This may or may not have an influence in nerd sniping me into writing that tool. In cases like these, Hapsland (or its approach, at least) comes to help. I know, I know, Abide (look it up!) exists, but I wanted (a) semantic expansion of code (b) full control over what's sent to Jev (hey, their ToS aren't that privacy-friendly) (c) less footprint on the file system. So I made it compatible. In case you want to use both, I mean. TLDR: catch a change with a coding agent hook => expand it into semantic code structure, respecting privacy settings => call Jev with your own code semantic rules => deliver feedback to the agent in the same turn, in 0.5s. P.S. This is a repost from last week when I was being a genius; I forgot to add "Show HN:" to the title, and then 30m passed and I couldn't delete that post anymore; renaming didn't put it into Show HN either.

projects.author: robertn702

github.name: robertn702/reasoning-router
github.description: Per-step reasoning effort for coding agents, picked by a classifier, without breaking the prompt cache. OpenCode plugin, Pi extension, and a local proxy for Codex CLI.

projects.summary: 我一直把编程 Agent 的推理强度开在 high，连改名这种小事也是，用量消耗得很快。但降到 medium 又会出错：在一个较难的 pytest bug 上，GPT-6 Astra 用 medium 5 次只解决了 1 次。 所以我做了 reasoning-router。编程 Agent 每次请求模型之前，它先让一个小型分类器（默认是 TypeSafe 的 Jev，也可以换成 Cloudflare Clef、Laya 等）判断这一步需要多少推理强度，再把结果加到请求里。 切换推理强度通常会让 prompt cache 失效。它用 OpenAI 的 configurationupdate 和 Anthropic 的对话中 effort 消息来改强度，之前的上下文不变，所以缓存还能命中。 在 10 个 SWE-bench Verified 问题上，路由和固定 high 都解决了 44/44，路由少用约 14% 的输出 token，耗时少约 9%。只测了一个模型和一组任务，结果仅供参考。 支持 OpenCode 插件、Pi 扩展，以及可接入 Codex CLI 的本地代理。目前是 alpha 版本，MIT 协议。

projects.title: [开源推荐] 让 AI 自己打断点：通用的 Java 远程调试 Agent Skill
projects.author: Aresxue

github.name: Aresxue/java-debug-skill
github.description: A Java remote breakpoint debugging Skill for AI agents such as Claude Code. It attaches to a remote JVM with JDWP enabled. The AI plans and sets breakpoints, waits for hits, collects call stacks and local variables, evaluates expressions and single-steps. It then reports a root cause based only on runtime data it actually collected.

projects.summary: java-debug 是一个 Java 远程断点调试 Agent Skill（标准 SKILL.md 格式），Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等支持 Skills 的 Agent 都能用。它会连接开启了 JDWP 的远程 JVM，由 AI 自行规划断点、等待命中，采集调用栈和局部变量，执行表达式求值和单步，最后根据实际采集到的运行时数据给出根因结论，而不是对着日志猜。核心是自研的 JDI 客户端：只依赖 JDK 内置的 com.sun.jdi，零外部依赖，以常驻 HTTP 服务模式运行，每个操作都是一条 JSON 命令，用 curl 就能驱动。 亮点 为 AI 驱动重新设计：jdb 输出的是文本，要靠 tmux + sleep 抢时序，而且默认冻结整个 JVM。这里改为 SUSPENDEVENTTHREAD，只冻结命中的线程；请求和响应都是结构化 JSON，命中时自动带回调用栈和局部变量，等待命中是带超时的阻塞等待。 断点不漏装：类还没加载时自动转为延迟断点；重载方法、同一行的多个可执行位置（包括 lambda）都会装上；多 ClassLoader 和热部署场景下，同名类的每个副本都装断点，之后加载的副本也会自动补装。 安全边界写成硬约束：命令端口只绑定 127.0.0.1，会校验 Host 头并拒绝浏览器跨站请求；eval 内置拒绝名单（System.exit、Runtime.exec 等）；命中时从不自动调用 toString()；disconnect 后被冻结的线程全部恢复。工作流还要求断点计划先经用户确认，结束时必须 disconnect。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Sax Design Vue：有亿点点不一样的 Vue3 组件库，内置强大的表格与 Agent 组件
projects.author: adoin

github.name: adoin/sax-design-vue
github.description: Beautiful Vue3 UI components base on Vuesax Vue2 version

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一下我一个人维护的开源项目 Sax Design Vue：基于 Vue3 和 TypeScript 的 UI 组件库，最近发布了 2.1.0，MIT 协议。 Vuesax 的 Vue3 版本停止持续更新后，我想尝试把它复活。做着做着，又决定在原有视觉语言上做点更大胆、更不一样的东西：让它既能做出有辨识度的界面，也能承接复杂数据业务与 Agent 应用。表格的功能和交互参考了 vxe-table，感谢这两个项目带来的启发。 特色目录 | 能力 | 值得一看的地方 | | --- | --- | | 基于路由的 Anchor | 同一份目录混合路由章节和页内锚点；支持页首 / 页尾继续滚动切换章节，以及相邻路由预取。 | | 动态行高与双向虚拟表格 | 根据内容测量实际行高，配合行列虚拟化和按索引数据源；固定列、多级表头等业务能力仍可组合使用。 | | Form / Table 共享渲染器 | 同一份渲染器定义服务于单元格展示、编辑、表单与筛选，复用标准控件和业务规则。 | | 14 个 Agent 交互组件 | 覆盖输入、消息、流式输出、推理步骤、引用、计划审批等过程；模型能力通过数据配置联动。 | | 液态镜片 Card | 用 SVG 滤镜实现背景折射，材质、布局和交互效果可以独立组合。 | | 弧形与 3D Carousel | 弧形扇面、卡片层叠、环形轨道和棱柱展示，共用导航、拖动和自动播放能力。 | | 暗水印与截图显影 | 除明水印外，也能生成低可见度的暗水印，并提供截图显影示例。 | | 声明式 Skeleton | 用圆、方块、长条与嵌套行的简易配置组合骨架屏，避免每种布局都手写占位结构。 | 下面用几个实际示例介绍其中的重点。 1. 有自己的美术风格 延续 Vuesax 的设计语言，以无边框、圆角、柔和阴影和渐变建立层次，强调卡片、控件、浮层之间的一致性；支持浅色 / 深色主题，也提供玻璃材质、气泡纹理进度条等视觉能力。 输入、选择、反馈和弹出层都沿用这套视觉语言，配合霓虹文字、材质和动效做一点大胆的尝试。 2. 表格的业务能力与大数据渲染一起做 Table 在同一个组件中提供多级表头、固定列、树形与分组、汇总、合并单元格、编辑校验、变更跟踪、查找替换、行列拖拽，以及查询表单、工具栏和请求代理。Form 与 Table 共用渲染器机制，常见输入与操作可以通过配置复用。 动态行高会按内容自动测量，支持换行文本与不同高度的行，并与行列虚拟化配合，不要求每一行都写死高度。 性能方面支持行列双向虚拟化和按索引数据源 virtualSource。虚拟化减少 DOM；索引数据源进一步避免为了描述巨量逻辑行列而先创建完整数组。 下面是文档中的 10 万行 × 10 万列逻辑数据示例，支持在起点、中部和末端之间跳转，只读取当前窗口，并保留固定列。它表示逻辑规模，不会一次创建或渲染全部单元格。文档还提供百万行生成源的校验与图表取数示例。 可以直接体验：表格基础 · 编辑与校验 · 虚拟化与大数据 3. 内置 14 个常用 Agent 交互组件 覆盖聊天输入、角色消息、消息虚拟滚动、聊天历史、流式文本、推理步骤、引用、代码块、文件差异、任务列表、计划审批、问题卡片、图像生成状态和 Agent Editor。 聊天输入：文件选择与图片预览、语音输入入口、模型选择、Fast 和思考强度设置；模型能力由应用传入，切换模型时联动可用选项。 消息与输出：用户 / Agent 的不同布局和操作，动态行高虚拟滚动、历史懒加载、流式展示和引用。 执行过程：推理步骤、任务列表、可展开的计划与批准反馈，以及收集用户回答的问题卡片。 这些组件负责界面和交互，模型服务及业务流程由应用接入。可以从现成组件开始组合，而不必逐个重写聊天与执行过程的基础 UI。 项目提供中英文文档、可运行示例、代码查看与在线 Playground。

projects.author: randomname123
projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Yk ，在 V2EX 一般只看帖，不怎么回复。这次分享一下自己天天在用的工具，希望能得到大家的反馈。 平时上班的时候或者下班 vibe ，都会 Claude Code/Codex/Cursor 混着用，一直有两个痛点： 1. 不同模型交互会有困难，经常需要我复制粘贴对话或者说一样的话； 2. 长任务卡让他们交互经常需要我来指引。 所以基于自己的工作流做了 Sealwire ，一个多 agent 协作工具。自己已经用了半年，感觉比较稳定了，发点测试码给有需要的朋友。 产品的初衷是能够花更少时间呆在电脑前面等待 Agent ，能有更多时间思考产品和陪伴家人。 演示视频： https://youtu.be/38TT8iX9Oqw 目前支持 - 支持五种 Harness：Claude Code 、Codex 、Cursor 、OpenCode 、Pi - 跨 agent review：/review ，你可以让一个 agent 审另外一个 agent 的改动。 - /goal 让 agent 自己跑到完成，/delegate 把支线任务丢给另一个 agent 。 - 默认是本地隐私模式。 - Cloud 模式下手机浏览器同一会话：PWA + 推送，可以远程审批，所有消息默认远程端到端加密。 https://i.imgur.com/vSD59A3.png https://i.imgur.com/9VWAj0g.png 如何开始：在项目目录跑 npx sealwire 说明： - 协议：PolyForm Internal Use + 个人使用许可，源码公开方便安全审计。个人和公司内部免费使用，不允许分发。详情请参考 Github 的 license 说明。 - 手机远程需要 SealWire Cloud access key ，用手机浏览器打开 https://app.sealwire.dev 即可。需要的朋友可以在帖子里回复 base64 编码后的邮箱，或者发邮件到 sealwire.dev@gmail.com （注明 V2EX ），我会发一年有效的 key 。目前短期内暂无收费计划。 - 目前只支持 macOS / Linux 。 - 接下来计划支持基于代码库上下文的语音输入，以及 iOS app 。 GitHub： https://github.com/sealwire/sealwire 问题和建议欢迎提 issue 或在帖子里回复，特别想听听大家对跨 agent review 流程的看法，以及你们平时管理多个 agent 的痛点。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】麦麦点餐最优解 - 用 Python 算清麦当劳优惠券的开源 Skill
projects.author: minxin88

github.name: minxin88/mcd-meal-optimizer
github.description: 麦麦点餐最优解 · WorkBuddy Skill × 麦当劳 MCP — 用本地组合优化引擎算出最省/最健康/性价比最高的点餐方案

projects.summary: 一个跑在 WorkBuddy 上的开源 Skill：接麦当劳中国官方 MCP，拉门店真实菜单、真实营养数据、真实可用优惠券，再用本地 Python 脚本穷举所有搭配，算出「最省 / 最健康 / 性价比最高」三套能直接下单的方案。 它只依赖 Python 标准库，不需要 pip install，也不需要 MCP Token 就能先跑一遍离线示例看效果。 为什么做这个项目？ 麦当劳的优惠券是满减、折扣、品类限定混着来的，单看每一张都懂，放在一起就不会算了。 举个真实的坑：手里有「满 40 减 10」和「汉堡 8.8 折」两张券。 买一个 25.5 元的汉堡：8.8 折省 3.06 元，满减用不了 → 折扣赢 买两个（51 元）：8.8 折省 6.12 元，满减省 10 元 → 满减赢 再加一份 12 元薯条凑到 63 元：薯条白买了 —— 券已经封顶在减 10，多花的 12 元一分没省 也就是说，哪张券最省、要不要凑单，完全取决于你这单的构成，没有标准答案。 再叠上「预算 45 元、热量不超 1100 kcal、蛋白质要 35 克以上」这类约束，满足条件的组合轻松上千套，人手不可能算完。 它是怎么工作的？ 核心设计是把「算」和「说」分开： 用户说人话 │ "两个人吃、50 块以内、别太油" ▼ 大模型理解意图 ──► 翻译成硬约束（预算/热量/蛋白质/忌口） │ ▼ 麦当劳 MCP 拉真实数据 ──► 门店菜单 / 营养 / 可用券 │ ▼ 本地 Python 脚本（无网络）──► 穷举全部组合 + 券最优匹配 │ ▼ 大模型组织成人话 ──► 三套方案 为什么不把枚举交给大模型？ 上千套组合的枚举是纯数学问题，不是语言问题。交给大模型：慢、贵、会算错钱；交给脚本：几毫秒出结果、可复现、零 token 消耗。 功能与特点 真实数据：菜单、价格、营养、优惠券全部来自麦当劳官方 MCP 实时接口，不内置任何硬编码数据表 券最优匹配：对每个组合遍历所有券，按「这一单实际能减多少」挑最省的那张（一张订单只能用一张券，不能简单挑面额大的） 三种口味排序：最省（实付升序）/ 最健康（热量蛋白质偏离度）/ 性价比（每 1 元换到的蛋白质克数） 零依赖：Python 3.9+，只用标准库，无网络请求 先试后配：内置离线示例数据，python scripts/optimizemeal.py --demo 无需 Token 即可跑出结果 有边界：不主动下单、不自动领券；涉及花钱的操作一律先让用户确认门店、取餐方式和商品清单 实测 2026-10-12 在深圳北站站内一店（早餐时段）真实跑过一次：约束为预算 ≤ 45 元、热量 ≤ 1100 kcal、蛋白质 ≥ 35 g，共枚举出 127 套可行组合，最省方案实付 29.4 元。

projects.title: Show HN: I Cut my Agent Tokens By 50%
projects.author: iohotspot
projects.summary: This started by watching the built-in tool calls in Claude code. We noticed that a LOT of the time was being spent searching for lines of code with regex. This approach makes sense when you are working in an unknown environment, but we all work inside of some codebase structure and tracking. This took us down the rabbit hole of codebase indexing and led to us building Indexio. Indexio was built to eliminate the time and tokens agents waste rediscovering a codebase. Regex calls return lots of data each time to the context window which causes bloat over time with items that don't really matter. Since codebase work container mostly static files indexing them and quickly getting to data for discovery is what we were trying to solve. Indexio index's the codebase to its internal DB and then returns what is needed via MCP when asked. We ran into some fun issues when trying to force the session to use a tool call for lookups so there is some aggressive tool call logic which attempts to override built-in lookup tools. If something isn't in the index it will just fallback to regex lookups. The whole system is a single binary written in Rust for performance. In our real world testing we are seeing about 50%-60% reduction in token usage compared to the built-in tools, and near instant lookup times compared to multiple seconds for each regex lookup. One place that indexio does come up shorter than then regex is when looking up symbols. We found that most of the agent's work was done looking at strings of words rather than symbols, but if you have a workflow that is heavy in this specific situation just know it may not fit. We opened sourced everything and would love to hear feedback. Huge Shout out to CocoIndex who gave us the inspiration for this idea. https://github.com/IOServicesLabs/indexio

projects.author: wx4766

github.name: wx4766/html-to-video
github.description: 用代码逐帧做视频：HTML / Canvas 动画 → MP4 / GIF / 透明层 · Deterministic HTML-to-MP4 renderer: seek to t, screenshot, encode. No framework, no build step, no GPU.

projects.summary: 一个把 HTML / Canvas 动画逐帧渲染成 MP4 的命令行工具。 不是录屏，也不是 AI 文生视频。做法是：把画面在 HTML 里写成 frame(t) 纯函数，用无头浏览器逐帧 seek 到指定时刻截图，再用 ffmpeg 编成 H.264。因为是逐帧推的，所以帧率是真的（60fps 不用插帧），每一帧都精确对齐，同样的输入永远得到同样的输出。 它解决的问题 现在想用代码做视频，主流选择是 Remotion（React）或 Motion Canvas（场景式）。两者都好，但要先把内容组织成它们的世界观。而很多真实场景是：手上已经有一屏 HTML（常常是 AI 刚生成的），只想把它变成 mp4。为一屏画面建一个 React 工程，代价过大。 这个工具刻意不做框架 —— 输入是一个能跑的 HTML 文件，输出是 mp4： bash bash assets/render.sh my-video.html --duration=6 --fps=60 几个不太常见的点 确定性：冻结 wall-clock rAF，由外部逐帧推进，同一份代码重跑逐帧一致。可版本管理、可做视觉回归 自带验收：qa.js 检查六维（确定性 / 最长连续静止 / 跳变 / 文字框景 / 字体回退 / 控制台报错）。为了让验收本身可信，仓库里放了一个塞满六类真实缺陷的对照样本，测试要求它必须被判失败 横竖屏自适应：--width=1080 --height=1920 就是竖屏，模板跟视口重排而不是拉伸。1920×1080 下与旧版逐像素一致（PSNR 逐帧回归，average:inf） 断点续渲：--resume，长片子跑到 80% 崩了不用从零开始。帧先写 .part 再改名，参数变了直接拒绝，编码前逐个核帧号 —— 实测续渲出来的 mp4 与一次渲完的 MD5 完全相同 MIT，纯本地运行，不调任何 API，不按次计费。

projects.title: Show HN: Cosplay as a tech lead, using gVisor to sandbox agents
projects.author: SftwareRenderer
projects.summary: Hi everyone, This started as an exploration into harnesses and locally hostable LLMs (the kind that uses less power than a small electric heater), and I used it as an opportunity to retool. I've tried popular ones like Cline, Claude Code, and Pi, but wanted a different UX and integrated sandboxes. The solution that I've landed on is a responsive web interface where I can quickly drive progress. It feels like a microcosm of my day job: define and delegate tasks, organize using kanban, then review deliverables. And it also feels like the time I used to spend coding is now spent in code review with the agent, so I tried to optimize the UX to make review feel nicer. One of my (maybe a bit niche) benchmark use-cases is how pleasant it is to make progress on hobby software projects while also out on a hike. This meant specifying low bandwidth usage and offline mode. Now I can jot down an idea, start the task, and at some point down the trail: get a notification* that either clarification is needed, a decision needs to be made, or the code is ready for review. I've been having a good time with this. To build MIKE, I exclusively used locally hostable LLMs (from Google, Meta, Qwen, Poolside, and DeepSeek) hosted with llama.cpp on my machines at home (Strix Halo and a 5090) to "compile" the code. The experience has gotten substantially better ever since DeepSeek’s release in July. Side note: I have a soft spot for llama.cpp since it was one of the first that made it possible to run this new tech at home, and its maintainers accepted a tiny improvement I made to error reporting. Oh the joys of having a PR get approved. I plan on maintaining this, at least until similar features are supported by better tools. Until then, hope you find this useful! 5 minute demo: https://youtu.be/jexzLkZ50FU p.s. I didn't mention details about the sandbox earlier since most people seem to find this a bit boring. It was one of my critical requirements, and I opted to use an existing battle-tested sandbox. I'm not an expert on how the Linux kernel works, but seeing all the VM escape exploits recently is a bit scary, and I liked gVisor’s approach to the problem. I'm also using Git worktrees to provision the agent’s workspace, as well as a read-only repository mount to provide relevant context when the agent looks for it. *off by default

projects.title: Show HN: CoastMath: (Open Source) Personal Finance and Retirement Planner
projects.author: jfrbfbreudh
projects.summary: Self-hosting instructions in the README. Hosted version: https://coastmath.com/ iOS app: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6809539979 This post is partially inspired by this thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50048344 ``` > Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. >> No, they can't, at least not any semblance of quality. The cases we're seeing where this does kinda work is in ports and translation where all the rules are already documented in the best specification language possible with a way for the LLM to verify itself: code. We saw this close to a year ago now with Cloudflare and NextJS ``` This post mostly outlines how I am personally building with agents, as I am almost entirely hands-off. Desired feature-set determined by having agents research existing products and feedback / feature requests on FIRE subreddits. Features built using Opus 5.5 (xhigh) / Fable 5.1 (med/high) as orchestrator and Opus-5-5 low/medium as worker subagents. Quality is attempted by running Opus-5-5 agents in a perpetual audit + fixer loop on the calculation / compliance engine until no medium+ severity can be found. The origin of each rule / logic must be backed up and documented in the codebase with a source. Sonnet subagents run UX / QA audit on iOS simulators within the Claude Code desktop app, and Opus agents resolve all medium+ sev issues; also run on a perpetual loop. I have not manually tested or used the app(s) for more than 30 minutes. For UX quality, agents' screenshots + associated context are fed to a combination of GPT / Gemini / Claude agents until consensus is achieved on quality (7/10+). Early feedback from beta testers report extremely close results to Boldin / Projection Lab. There is also a feature to import your data from Boldin and Projection Lab into CoastMath if you wish to compare the results yourself. There is also a SimpleFIN integration, if you wish to pull in your own transaction data and see how your financial future changes based on your monthly spending habits (e.g. when I will get to retire if I spend like I did in June vs. July?). I'm sure there are other features I don't yet know about. Again, I've barely used the app. Anyway, feel free to use / roast / steal. I don't think that any moat can exist in this class of products in the future (where the rules are laws that are visible to everyone) and I don't expect to turn a profit. Estimated cost: maybe $2000 if done over the API? I did most of this using the $200 Max subscription.

projects.summary: 「把周会挪到周五下午三点，标成高优先级。」——在 AI Todo 里，你对输入框说的每一句话，都会先变成一条 diff：改哪个任务、改成什么，一目了然。你确认，它才动手。 这个设计同时回应两个现实：一是表单式 todo 太累，日期选择器、优先级下拉、标签面板，记个事要填八个字段——LLM 时代，输入框应该只剩一个；二是 AI 不该直接碰你的数据，它理解得再好也有翻车的时候，diff 预览是安全底线，用下来也意外成了「AI 在想什么」的透明窗口。 它还有一半是为 AI agent 造的：CLI 全 JSON 输出，agent 读 --help 就能自己学会全部命令——我自己搭的 AI 助手每天都通过它记待办、排事项，它是我少数自己每天都在吃狗粮的项目。 任务支持多层嵌套，任务列表可升级为共享项目空间（@成员 + 甘特图）。自托管，MIT。

projects.summary: Endo is a Higher-Order Harness (HOH). From the easiest concept to understand to the more complex ones, Endo gives you: * A single, simple UI to use any agent provider with your existing subscriptions, and hot-swap agents right in the middle of a session. * An orchestration layer, which I call HOH, allowing arbitrary composition of agents to achieve any workflow. A fun case I tried was asking Fable and Astra to mock a presidential debate. * An agent protocol that abstracts any agent. The key insight here is that every LLM is an agent—instead of treating the LLM as just one node inside an external ReAct loop. Endo was a concept formed while I was building OpenChart ( https://github.com/longsurf-ai/openchart ). To power trading workflows, I needed to support scenarios where strict determinism is required, while still keeping the flexibility of an agent's inference-time decision-making capability. A new form factor was needed between rigid n8n-style workflows and open-ended ReAct loop agents. Thus the creation of Endo. Endo is short for Endomorphism, a term rooted in category theory and functional programming. An endomorphism is a function that transforms an object into another object of the same type. Similarly, Endo itself is built purely on functional programming principles, relying heavily on Effect ( https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect ). ..And if you have patience to speak technical jargons, Endo is: * An agent orchestration layer—Higher-Order Harness (HOH)—where an entire agent is treated the same as a single LLM call, enabling arbitrary composition of extremely complex workflows. * A way to abstract any harness into a standardized protocol, where raw models and agents behave the exact same way, in a KV-cache-friendly manner. * A workflow engine that enables arbitrary composition of agents with a single workflow language. It's completely open source, and if you think this idea is cool, let's build together. Just for the fun of it.

projects.title: Show HN: Beeline Multiplayer Agent Harness

We built beeline itself with early versions of beeline, and use it to build our other projects - it's boosted productivity quite a bit for us. This has led to people having to forward AI slop to each other or to try to deliver context through various shims like meetings or task tickets. Beeline is a single control plane for your entire team, both human and agent, and is designed to help your team do its best work. Things to expect: - This is a multiplayer agentic harness, not a slack substitute. It's best for focused product teams doing or relying on engineering tools and shipping code. - Open source and not a business. We use beeline internally, and just thought it would be a really cool thing to exist in the world. There are still lots of bugs - Sweepstakes things like computer use, lots of third party connector integrations are there. What's cool is that beeline agents can automate _auth_ through trustysquire.ai - they can sign up to most services and APIs without you having to do it for them. - A new primitive called workflows, that are skills for teams of agents. - multi way call with your entire team, humans and agents.
